title: Do AI generated 3D models contain some sort of a way that a user can decompile the file and find proof that the asset were made using ai? (Tripo / any other 3D modeling software)
author: Fluid-Tap5115
selftext:
I am interested in using assets from this website called Tripo, as I am really good with concept art, but am awful at actually making 3d models 

I thought tripo might be a match made in heaven, and might be great way to still make a 3D game without sacrificing my artistic vision by working with outsiders that don't entirely understand what I am looking for

That said, AI is very looked down upon and I do want to work with artists to refine my models, but am super worried that they will hate me if I use AI models   
  
(some work for free as they want to be part of the project for no pay, and thus, I dont want to disrespect them)  
  
aside form the people helping me make these assets, there are also the fans, that may look far too two dimensionally at the thought of me using AI to make my models, and thus, might reflect unintended hate on what I make   
  
I don't want to pose my art as purely made by AI, but feel like if I say that my work does contain assets made using AI, my human artist purist helpers might stop supporting my work  
  
Regardless

TLDR: Can somebody decompile a Tripo model I have used in my game, and find out that I used AI 3D model art in my game?

comments.author: TruWaves
comments.body: Just open the models in a 3d editor and rename everything that says tripo.

comments.author: Olmeca_Gold
comments.body:
These neural networks generate 3d models with point clouds. Thats a different workflow compared to working with blender etc. So they typically will include cues that will be discernable even when looking at them. And people can extract and verify from topography. So yes to your question.

If you have the means to hire an artist no reason not to commission a non AI workflow. If you want to use AI models you need to bite the bullet and have a strategy on how you plan to deal with the anti AI zealots.

comments.author: kessler_explosions
comments.body: Fuck em, make your game, its your vision, realize it with whatever tools you have at your disposal.

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body: That’s what I am saying. Who gives a f. If there is a Tool I Can use to safe time and Money, I will use it

replies.author: TicklishBubbles
replies.body:
Unfortunately, many people instantly dislike anything created using AI. I, on the other hand don't care by which means something was created, as long as I can enjoy the result. Hell, even some AI songs are much better than what nonsense is being played on the radio daily. 

I agree with you. Don't give a F about what people think. Enjoy the endless possibilities of creating something you've always dreamed of doing.

replies.author: M4xs0n
replies.body:
Exactly. People act like using AI suddenly makes your work less real or less creative, but that’s just ego talking. A lot of them romanticize this idea of “I have to do everything myself for ‘real’ or it doesn’t count,” and then get mad when others don’t follow that mindset and they stay behind.

In the end nobody cares how something was made. If a tool helps you get the result you want faster or better, why wouldn’t you use it? That’s literally what progress is. AI won‘t take their jobs, but people who use AI tools will.

comments.author: CouchOtter
comments.body: Are you generating assets or characters that need to be rigged so they can deform and animate? This is where you’ll likely run into issues. There’s a reason why you rarely see wireframes of generated assets, just beauty frames of rendered images or 3D prints. With organic characters, you need proper topology with clean edge loops at the joints, not a dense mesh of tris that look like a photogrammetry scan. That won’t deform well, and would likely be a visual cue that the assets are gen AI. If you need a team to help deliver your project, just be upfront about the source material.

comments.author: nck_pi
comments.body: A 3d artist will most likely recognize ai made meshes just from topology

replies.author: MapleTrust
replies.body: Lol Kel not there game sales demographic, bit I agree.

comments.author: ThaBombs
comments.body:
3d artists could probably see the odd topography of the ai work. I haven't looked into 3d AI models and it has been a few years since I last sculpted models myself, but zbrush has a few tricks that can remesh/automatically refine the topology. I think it was called z-remesher, I never really used it as it distorted some details. However it did clean the topology up nicely.

Can't tell you if it's foolproof and hides it perfectly, but you can always try.

comments.author: Fluid-Tap5115
comments.body:
To sort of clarify what I am making 

My work is specifically 3000-1000 poly count size wise, and to me, a non 3d modeler, feels like something that doesn't look AI at a first glance

What I am worried about is the internal stuff that I am too new to understand, and might miss when generating models with Tripo

replies.author: justifun
replies.body: As soon as you retopologoze it then you've made a new mesh so you won't need the original anymore.  Think of it more like using the ai model like you would if you traced a photograph onto a piece of paper.  Just in 3d.

comments.author: IncorrectAddress
comments.body: Not what I've seen from so far, so if AI built the high poly model, and then you poly chop and fix any topology issues, it's good to go as being called your own, a simple way to check is to export the model to OBJ then check the file for any extra crapola (which you could edit manually if you like).

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body: Embedded identifiers, such as there could be double vertices onto of each other that could contain floating data that when combined could provide an identifier, but any 3D artist would notice this off the bat in something like blender or the file type, so it would only be those that export something and just use it as is where it could be maybe seen within the file, but I doubt that's being done in generation.

replies.author: Fluid-Tap5115
replies.body:
is there really no internal parts on the inside of a model that make it detectable to have been made by AI?

I had asked about this elsewhere and they said that the wireframe could also give it away

but am still learning what all of those mean

My biggest issue rn is that the obj and fbx files i am downloading off of Tripo arent opening in blender lol

replies.author: IncorrectAddress
replies.body: There maybe commonalities in the AI output of the mesh, but they won't stand out or be applicable to saying this is from this.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
This kind of thing is similar to the stupid argument people used to have and many still have, about CG in movies.

Most people have no idea how CG is made and so see it as easy and a low effort cheap shortcut because they think the computer is doing all the work.

What actually happens is that 90% of CG in movies and shows goes completely unnoticed and nobody cares. People only care and complain when it looks like low quality CG.

There's no difference between that and using AI. If your output looks like low quality AI people will notice and will complain. If your AI is so good nobody can even tell it was used, nobody but a tiny minority will care.

If you can't use AI in a way that it doesn't look like obvious AI then you probably shouldn't use it. 

People in general will always be far less forgiving about the quality of something the less effort they perceive went into it.

comments.author: locustbill
comments.body: You can retopo and remesh to get better edge flow if that is a concern.

comments.author: Critical_Task_9763
comments.body: Just manual retopo and nothing can carry over cuz its a complete new mesh. Literally impossible to know after that
